Backstory:

One year and one day ago I decided to go to a trampoline park with a couple of my college buddies. We get there, everything is cool, mostly kids but no one is getting in anyone else's way. Anyway, there's a section where you can jump from these trampolines into a foam pit. I used to be very good on the trampoline back when I was a kid, so I figure I can get some good air before landing in the foam pit. On one jump, I was getting a lot of air and jumped forward towards the foam pit, but I guess I put too much torque on my leg. I remember hearing a loud snap, like when a tree branch breaks, and then landing and looking down at my leg. No skin had broken, but it was clear as day what had happened.

There wasn't any pain, but my leg felt like it was getting hot and cold at the same time. I asked for my phone so I could take a picture while the workers called an ambulance in for my dumb ass. They gave me a large shot of morphine, then tried moving my 190 lb self out of the foam pit. It took 6 people, and at one point they dropped the lower part of my leg. Next thing I know, I'm in an ambulance, high as shit on morphine but still totally aware of everything.

I had surgery later that night and spent a week in the hospital before getting released. A rod and four screws were thrown in my leg, and I got a nasty blood infection when I was in there because they left the IV in the same spot for almost four days. I could put some weight on the leg about two weeks later, but couldn't walk at all on it for about two months, and even that was a pretty stupid looking limp.

It's been one year and one day since the break, and I can lift weights again and walk totally normally. Running still hurts, mostly at the knee, but I can somewhat jog. I'm just glad that it's almost back to normal.
